answer: At a cedar check-in booth, a lantern reveals a fresh coordinate on a printed nebula map; an independent steward checks a participant in person, issues only one stamped credential per person, and records that coordinate on it. The verifier accepts a credential only if its steward signature, unique serial, and epoch coordinate match the booth log. To multiply accounts, a cheater must bring a different accomplice to the booth for every extra credential, paying each person's time and travel rather than spinning up free wallets.
